automation_turned_off.name: Automation turned off
automation_turned_off.description: Fires when somebody, or something, turns an automation off. Leave the target empty to watch every automation.

debounce.name: Once it settles
debounce.description: Fires once a trigger has stopped firing for a while, so a burst of them arrives as one. A motion sensor does not report motion once, it reports it twenty times.

triggers.name: Triggers
triggers.description: The triggers to wait out. Any of them firing starts a burst and any of them firing again keeps it going, so several triggers are collapsed together rather than one at a time.

for.name: For
for.description: How long it has to have been quiet before this fires. Every firing starts that wait over, so something that never stops firing never gets reported.

all_of.name: All of these happened
all_of.description: Fires when every one of several triggers has fired inside the same window of time, in any order. Home Assistant's own triggers are a list where any one of them is enough; this is the other one.

triggers.name: Triggers
triggers.description: The triggers that all have to have fired. Order does not matter, and a trigger firing again replaces its earlier turn rather than counting twice.

within.name: Within
within.description: How close together they have to be. The window slides, so a trigger that fired longer ago than this is forgotten while the others carry on counting.

recovered.name: Entity came back
recovered.description: Fires when an entity comes back after having been unavailable for a while, so a router rebooting does not read as everything in the house recovering.

for.name: For
for.description: How long the entity has to have been away before coming back counts. Anything shorter is a flicker: reloading an integration takes every one of its entities through unavailable and back inside a second.

device_added.name: Device added
device_added.description: Fires when a new device is added to Home Assistant, like a plug that was just paired.

sequence.name: Triggers in order
sequence.description: Fires when several triggers happen one after another, in the order given.

steps.name: Steps
steps.description: The triggers that have to happen, in order. Only the one being waited for is listening, so a later step firing early is not a match.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: How long the whole sequence may take, counted from the first step. Left out, it waits indefinitely.

reset.name: Reset
reset.description: Triggers that abandon a sequence already under way, putting it back to waiting for the first step.

while.name: While a condition holds
while.description: Fires when a condition turns true, and keeps firing on an interval for as long as it stays true.

condition.name: Condition
condition.description: The condition to watch. Firing starts when it turns true and stops when it stops being true.

every.name: Every
every.description: How long to wait between one firing and the next, for as long as the condition holds.

watchdog.name: Watchdog
watchdog.description: Fires when something that was expected to happen does not happen in time.

arm.name: Arm
arm.description: What starts the watch. The wait is measured from here, and arming again while already waiting starts the wait over.

expect.name: Expect
expect.description: What is expected to follow. Arriving in time calls the watch off, and nothing fires.

within.name: Within
within.description: How long the expected thing has to arrive. This fires when that time passes and it has not.

flapping.name: Entity will not settle
flapping.description: Fires when an entity changes state more often than it should within a stretch of time.

changes.name: Changes
changes.description: How many changes of state it takes before this fires. Changes of attribute do not count, and neither does an entity appearing or disappearing.

within.name: Within
within.description: The stretch of time those changes have to fall inside. It slides along, so this is always about the most recent changes.

condition_met.name: Condition turned true
condition_met.description: Fires when a condition goes from false to true, using the same condition building blocks as anywhere else.

cron.name: Cron schedule
cron.description: Fires on a crontab schedule, for the times Home Assistant's own time triggers cannot express, like every weekday at seven or the last Friday of the month.

schedule.name: Schedule
schedule.description: A crontab expression with five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. Supports ranges and steps, and the day-of-week extensions, so "MON#2" is the second Monday and "5L" the last Friday. Nicknames like "@daily" are not supported.

device_discovered.name: Device discovered
device_discovered.description: Fires when Home Assistant discovers something new it could set up, like a device that just turned up on your network.

integration_added.name: Integration added
integration_added.description: Fires when an integration is added to Home Assistant, whoever or whatever added it.

integration_failed.name: Integration failed to set up
integration_failed.description: Fires when a configuration entry has been unable to set itself up for a while, past the point where Home Assistant's own retries would have sorted it out.

for.name: For
for.description: How long an entry has to keep failing before this fires. Home Assistant retries a failing entry every ten minutes at the slowest, so anything shorter than that reports trouble that may still fix itself.

entry_id.name: Entries
entry_id.description: Limit this to particular configuration entries. Leave it empty to watch every one of them.

repair_issue_created.name: Repair issue created
repair_issue_created.description: Fires when a new repair issue turns up, so you can hear about one without visiting the repairs page.

domain.name: Integrations
domain.description: Limit this to issues reported by particular integrations, by their domain. Leave it empty for all of them.

severity.name: Severity
severity.description: Limit this to issues of a particular severity. Leave it empty for all of them.

repair_issue_removed.name: Repair issue resolved
repair_issue_removed.description: Fires when a repair issue goes away, either fixed or no longer reported.

domain.name: Integrations
domain.description: Limit this to issues reported by particular integrations, by their domain. Leave it empty for all of them.

stale.name: Entity fell silent
stale.description: Fires when nothing has written to an entity for a while, which catches a device that died quietly rather than going unavailable.

for.name: For
for.description: How long an entity has to stay silent before this fires. An entity that keeps reporting the same value is not silent.

target_temperature_reached.name: Target temperature reached
target_temperature_reached.description: Fires when the temperature of a thermostat or water heater reaches its target, or jumps past it. Changing the target does not count, and neither does a device that is off.

tolerance.name: Tolerance
tolerance.description: How close to the target still counts as there, in the device's unit. For a thermostat that settles just short of its setpoint. Zero means the target itself.

update_installed.name: Update installed
update_installed.description: Fires when an update entity reports a different installed version, whether somebody pressed install, the device updated itself, or it was updated outside of Home Assistant.

position_reached.name: Position reached
position_reached.description: Fires when a cover or valve gets to a position, or moves past it. One that is already there, or comes back from unavailable at it, does not count.

position.name: Position
position.description: The position to reach, from 0 (closed) to 100 (open).

script_started.name: Script started
script_started.description: Fires when a script starts a run. A run the script refuses, because it is already running, does not count. Leave the target empty to watch every script.

user_added.name: User added
user_added.description: Fires when somebody is given a login to Home Assistant. Users Home Assistant creates for its own integrations are left out.

state_changed.name: Spook's state trigger
state_changed.description: Fires when an entity changes state, for everything a target covers: entities, devices, areas, floors and labels. Narrow it down by domain, integration or device class, or leave the target empty and let those pick the entities from everything. Exclude things again, and decide how long a change has to hold before it counts.

domain.name: Domains
domain.description: Only entities of these domains, like binary_sensor or cover. Without a target, picks them from everything.

integration.name: Integrations
integration.description: Only entities provided by these integrations, like zha or hue. Without a target, picks them from everything.

config_entry.name: Integration entry
config_entry.description: Only entities of this integration entry. Without a target, picks them from everything.

device_class.name: Device classes
device_class.description: Only entities of these device classes, like door or window. Without a target, picks them from everything.

exclude_target.name: Exclude
exclude_target.description: Entities, devices, areas, floors or labels to exclude. Everything in them is excluded, the diagnostic entities too.

exclude_domain.name: Exclude domains
exclude_domain.description: Exclude entities of these domains. With nothing in Exclude, this applies to everything the target covers.

exclude_integration.name: Exclude integrations
exclude_integration.description: Exclude entities provided by these integrations.

exclude_config_entry.name: Exclude integration entry
exclude_config_entry.description: Exclude the entities of this integration entry.

exclude_device_class.name: Exclude device classes
exclude_device_class.description: Exclude entities of these device classes.

attribute.name: Attribute
attribute.description: Follow this attribute instead of the state.

from.name: From
from.description: Only changes coming from one of these states.

not_from.name: Not from
not_from.description: Only changes not coming from one of these states.

to.name: To
to.description: Only changes going to one of these states.

not_to.name: Not to
not_to.description: Only changes not going to one of these states.

ignore_unavailable.name: Ignore unavailable and unknown
ignore_unavailable.description: Leave out changes from or to unavailable and unknown, so a restart or a router reboot does not fire for everything. Turn off to use them in From or To.

attribute_changes.name: Count attribute changes
attribute_changes.description: Also fire when only an attribute changed and the state stayed the same. Does nothing while following an attribute.

behavior.name: Behavior
behavior.description: Fire for each entity, for the first one of the target to get there, or once all of them are there. First and all need To or Not to. While unavailable and unknown are ignored, entities in those states do not take part.

for.name: For
for.description: Only fire once the new state has held for this long. Any other change in between calls it off.

blip_tolerance.name: Blip tolerance
blip_tolerance.description: While waiting out For, going unavailable or unknown and coming back as it was within this time does not start the wait over. Only works together with For.

delay.name: Delay
delay.description: Wait this long before firing, whatever happens in between. Like a delay at the start of the actions.

is_at_target_temperature.name: Temperature at its target
is_at_target_temperature.description: Passes when the temperature of a thermostat or water heater is at its target. A device that is off is not at its target, and one that is unavailable is left out.

behavior.name: Behavior
behavior.description: Whether any of the devices being there is enough, or all of them have to be.

tolerance.name: Tolerance
tolerance.description: How close to the target still counts as there, in the device's unit. For a thermostat that settles just short of its setpoint. Zero means the target itself.

repair_issue_present.name: Repair issue outstanding
repair_issue_present.description: Passes while a repair issue is outstanding. Issues somebody has ignored do not count.

domain.name: Integrations
domain.description: Limit this to issues reported by particular integrations, by their domain. Leave it empty for all of them.

severity.name: Severity
severity.description: Limit this to issues of a particular severity. Leave it empty for all of them.

quota.name: Run allowance left
quota.description: Passes while this automation has run fewer than a given number of times within a given period. Scripts are not counted.

limit.name: Limit
limit.description: How many runs are allowed within the period.

period.name: Period
period.description: The window the limit applies to. It rolls, so a day means any twenty-four hours rather than between midnights.

triggered_by_automation.name: Triggered by an automation
triggered_by_automation.description: Passes when another automation set this run going, whether it did so directly or through a script.

automation.name: Automations
automation.description: Limit this to particular automations. Leave it empty to accept any of them.

triggered_by_user.name: Triggered by a user
triggered_by_user.description: Passes when a person is behind what set this off: a state change or an event they caused, including one that made a template trigger become true. A schedule, the sun, or an integration acting on its own carries nobody, and neither does forcing a run with the Run button.

person.name: People
person.description: Only pass when one of these people started it. Leave empty to pass for anyone. A person has to have a user account linked to them, otherwise there is nothing to match against.

not_triggered_by_user.name: Not triggered by a user
not_triggered_by_user.description: Passes when nobody can be held responsible for this run: a schedule, the sun, an integration acting on its own, or the Run button. Takes no options on purpose. To exclude specific people instead, put "Triggered by a user" inside a Not condition.

chance.name: Chance
chance.description: Passes a set percentage of the time, chosen at random each check. Handy for adding a bit of variation to your automations.

percentage.name: Percentage
percentage.description: How often this condition should pass, as a percentage.

cooldown.name: Cooldown
cooldown.description: Passes only if this automation or script has not run within the given time (or has never run). A built-in cooldown, so it does not re-fire too often.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long to wait after the last run before this condition passes again.
